niche.habitat: 10–22 km altitude, within convective storm anvils and fair-weather electrostatic layers. Also, in the council's sketch (no such creature in this world yet): Ochre-grazer, cleans ectoparasites using conductive shock; grazers follow storm tracks for safety.
niche.diet: Chemosynthetic sulfate aerosols, lightning-ionized nitrates, electrochemical metabolites

body: 1.8 m hollow geodesic frame of conductive iron-sulfide and chitin, three buoyant gas bladders, electrostatic discharge nodes along the dorsal ridge

chains.trait: Posterior decoy detaches on lightning strike
links: Atmospheric electric field reaches 3 kV/m during storms

skill.effect: The creature sheds a decoy from its rear and launches itself high into the air, leaving the false form behind to draw attention.

chains.weakness: Grounded by heavy rain or low-humidity air; decoy drifts away and must be regrown over 3 days
observe: Gap forms between torso and tail

journal.en: It throws away its own tail just to run away.

plausibility.summary: Reframe as corona-proximity autotomy: dorsal nodes concentrate charge; rapid shedding drops mass and a posterior ‘decoy’ bearing higher curvature—thrust from elastic recoil + updraft, not repulsion alone. Direct strikes remain a rare fatality; gameplay ‘Charge Leap’ triggers on field surge + storm updraft, not on being the strike channel.

links: Sulfur-rich volcanic outgassing and high crustal radiation

skill.effect: Arcs of lightning travel along its iron-rich body and crackle outward, jolting nearby creatures and leaving them strongly disoriented.

chains.weakness: Poor insulation in calm air; slow recharge without storm proximity, easily disrupted by water

journal.en: Its bones are just lightning rods.

links: Emission peaks at 480 nm for atmospheric transmission
Ochre haze scatters yellow-red light but transmits blue-green
Aerosol extinction shifts skylight to ochre, leaving blue-green window

skill.effect: A soft blue-green glow pulses from its body, casting a visible aura that claims the area or soothes approaching rivals.

chains.weakness: Useless in thick fog or direct sunlight; attracts photo-sensitive predators and competitors

journal.en: It paints the sky with cold fire.

plausibility.summary: World canon (F23) already selects blue-green (470–520 nm) emitters active dusk-to-night because ochre forward scattering (F10) swamps longer wavelengths by day while a blue-green transmission window opens after dark. A stratospheric social/signaling flash at ~480 nm is the same physical logic as pelagic bioluminescence, only shifted upward in habitat.

chains.weakness: Clogged by heavy rain or high dust; requires constant updraft maintenance or ground roosting

plausibility.summary: State diet as heterotrophy on sky-reef-derived aggregates plus symbiont-supplied carbon in gut crypts; membranes trap microbial biofilms on sulfate dust, not ‘eating rock dust’ directly. Tie ‘Siphon Draft’ stamina regen to storm updrafts (F11) that concentrate particles. Note metabolic ceiling: filter area and calm-air clogging (rain/dust) are real limits at 1.36 g if the animal ever roosts at the surface.

body_plan.origin: pelagic-epipelagic filter-feeder lineage that colonized the upper troposphere

temperament: Cautiously reactive, highly sensitive to charge gradients, generally non-predatory unless grounded
secrets: The 'decoy' tail is not waste; it is a dormant embryo that hatches into a juvenile when it lands in a nutrient-rich thermal.
Their conductive lattice can be harvested as a stable, room-temperature superconductor if flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen.
They do not fear the storm; they wait for it, because without the charge, their hearts stop pumping.
moments: When the first lightning of the season strikes, the entire sky reef shivers, and thousands of them shed their tails in unison, a silent, ozone-scented storm of flying decoys.

journal.en: Not built to endure. Built to leap.
The sky is not empty; it is a charged reef.
